findings.action: The assignment replaces the resolver just rebound by withGovernanceReadView with store.FederatedResolver. In production, governance_read_view.go:708-713 supplies a resolver whose FS and Roots belong to the caller's operation. BuildIndexFederatedMaterialIn copies that resolver, and ArtifactResolver.resolve uses its FS and Roots for dependency policies, specs, transfers and revisions. Those observations therefore enter the caller's operation rather than isolated.operation. materialReadsSince collects only isolated.operation, and isolated.audit cannot prove the omitted dependency inputs. A later operation with unchanged local inputs and roots can reuse the old digest after a foreign dependency changes, without replaying or auditing that dependency. This violates R1-R3 and the retained-input integrity boundary. Preserve the isolated resolver binding and add a real federated-builder regression covering a changed foreign dependency and its presence in the replayed closure. The current tests replace the builder with a single local-file read and cannot detect this.

The isolated build inherits op.baseStore.Root, which is the coordinator root, rather than store.Root. governanceReadViewOperation.indexInputBinding explicitly invokes this path for foreign stores at governance_read_view.go:695-713. For such a call, the following assignment installs the foreign project ID while leaving the coordinator root selected. beginGovernanceReadView detects that project/root conflict, but build(scoped) still runs against the coordinator before the audit rejects retention and the caller performs its own build. Every foreign-root validation consequently performs a discarded build and cannot retain its own material. Select the requested store root while preserving the base filesystem binding, and test foreign-root validation within a coordinator operation.

The key identifies only successful project-to-root lookups, the local project and engine version. Material also depends on resolver outcomes that require no filesystem read. ArtifactResolver.resolve checks Authorize before lookup and emits unauthorized-project versus unknown-project for a referenced but unregistered project. Two operations with identical registered roots but different authorization of that unregistered project therefore have identical keys and replayable file closures, yet different material projections. Likewise, StoreFor errors are omitted at lines 131-134, losing conflicting-binding state. A hit can return the earlier projection digest without reevaluating these outcomes. Bind the retained entry to the relevant authorization and registry outcomes, or decline reuse when those semantic inputs cannot be replayed.
